items.title: Bitbase Launches ORIGIN, a Points Season That Rewards Consistency
items.summary: PANAMA CITY, November 4, 2026 — Bitbase today launched ORIGIN, the first season of its Bitbase Points program, which is designed to reward sustained participation over time. Over the 26-week season, which ends on May 4, 2027, Bitbase will distribute 1,000,000 points each week, allocated daily according to each participant’s contribution. Four sources of contribution Each participant’s contribution is drawn from four sources: trading, assets held on Bitbase, consistent activity and referrals. items.title: U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, September 2026
items.summary: The U.S. goods and services trade deficit decreased in September 2026 according to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis and the U.S. Census Bureau. The deficit decreased from $105.7 billion in August (revised) to $105.0 billion in September, as exports increased more than imports. The goods deficit decreased $0.7 billion in September to $135.9 billion. The services surplus decreased less than $0.1 billion in September to $30.9 billion.

items.title: September job openings, hires, and total separations change little; quits increase
items.summary: The number of job openings was little changed at 7.5 million in September. Hires and total separations changed little at 5.4 million and 5.3 million, respectively. Quits increased to 3.4 million, while layoffs and discharges changed little at 1.6 million.

items.title: Bitbase launches ORIGIN, distributing 1M points every week
items.summary: Panama City, November 4, 2026 — Bitbase today launched ORIGIN, the first season of its new Bitbase Points program. Ahead of the launch, the digital asset exchange credited points to eligible users who had been trading on the platform, so their past activity counts from day one. The season runs for 26 weeks, until May 4, 2027, with 1,000,000 points distributed each week. Part of Bitbase 2.0 ORIGIN is also the first part of Bitbase 2.0 to reach users directly.
